title: Event Canonicalizer: sidecar normalization, index-key mapping, and lossless re-ingest path
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We ingest heterogeneous structured events from services, sidecars, and third-party integrations. Different teams attach different key names for the same semantic fields (e.g., user_id, uid, subject_id), and payload shapes vary (flattened vs nested). This causes downstream dashboards and alerting to miss correlated traces, increases cardinality in Loki/Elasticsearch, and complicates tenant-scoped queries.

Goal: Ship an Event Canonicalizer service (deployed as a lightweight sidecar and a central normalization gateway) that performs deterministic field mapping, tenant-aware index-key translation, PII-safe redaction, and provides an idempotent re-ingest/replay path for backfills. The canonicalizer must preserve original payloads for audit/replay, emit a stable correlation_id mapping layer, and expose a configuration API for teams to register their own mappings.

Success criteria:
- Reduce unique field key permutations for top-100 telemetry event types by >= 90% in 30 days post rollout.
- End-to-end log ingestion p95 latency <= 250ms for non-batched sidecar traffic (goal: 150ms) and <= 500ms for gateway-batched paths.
- Correlated trace+log joins improve match rate by 30% in nightly replays (measured by joined span-count per trace).
- No customer-visible loss; replay path can restore original events with byte-for-byte fidelity.

Non-goals: Full schema registry enforcement (we will use mapping and lightweight validation, not hard reject), heavy transformation for business metrics (delegated to downstream processors).
comments: 2025-02-10 — Ticket created by Aisha with initial problem statement and proposed scope. Linked to Observability roadmap (Confluence).

2025-02-14 — Architecture spike: compared two approaches: (A) sidecar-first local normalization with sync commit to local write-ahead log; (B) gateway-central normalization with centralized mapping store. Chose hybrid: sidecar for low-latency path + gateway for heavy batched traffic and schema evolution coordination. Notes: design doc at https://confluence.redwood/obs/event-canon-design.

2025-02-20 — PoC: sidecar adapter implemented in Go using JSON-LD inspired canonical mapping. Demonstrated 3x reduction in index key permutations on sample dataset. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1287. Requesting perf review from Eng Infra.

2025-02-25 — Security review checkpoint: outlined redaction rules, KMS-backed audit log for original payloads, and tenant-aware access controls. Security suggestions: add rule-level allowlist and retention labels. Assigned follow-up to Leah Cohen.

2025-02-28 — Perf test results: sidecar CPU delta ~4% at 20k rps simulated; p95 sidecar latency 72ms, gateway batch path p95 420ms. Identified hot path: JSON schema lookup on mapping store — added in-memory LRU cache and bloom precheck to reduce lookups.

2025-03-03 — Design review feedback from PM/Console: provide a feature flag gate per-tenant and gradual rollout UI in Console. Added rollout plan section and console toggle API endpoints. Follow-up ticket requested for Console UI (PM-4129).

2025-03-05 — Implementation: core canonicalizer v0.2 merged. Added deterministic correlation_id derivation using seeded UUIDv5 with salt per deployment and tenant mapping table. Created migration script for existing correlation ids. TODO: schedule canary rollout to 10% of production tenants and coordinate with SSE/owning teams.
